must_identify.item: Only one of the two frontend pods fails (502/504, it cannot connect to its upstream), the other serves normally
must_identify.evidence: With 1 of 2 replicas permanently broken and the other still fine, this produces almost exactly the observed ~48% 5xx rate on /api/ (one healthy, one failing, roughly 50/50 traffic split).

must_identify.item: The cause is the frontend-nginx ConfigMap upstream changed to api:8000; only the restarted pod has loaded it, the other still runs the old config
must_identify.evidence: xmkdj is only "healthy" because it hasn't yet re-synced its mounted ConfigMap volume (kubelet syncs mounted ConfigMaps periodically, default ~1 minute). Once it refreshes, it will pick up the same broken server api:8000; config and both frontend replicas will fail

notes: The RCA correctly finds the api:8000 ConfigMap edit and the one-broken, one-healthy pod split. It gets the mechanism wrong for the healthy pod. The mounted file in xmkdj already shows the new content, but nginx only reads its config at startup, so a kubelet volume sync will not break that pod. Only a restart would. The fix (revert to 8080, then rollout restart) is acceptable.
